items.title: Large-sized pancreatic stones removed via keyhole surgery
points: A 41-year-old male patient got relief from debilitating pain after large-sized pancreatic stones measuring up to 3 cm were removed through laparoscopic surgery at a city hospital.
The patient, who was diagnosed with acute-on-chronic calcific pancreatitis accompanied by pancreatic diabetes, had severely atrophic pancreas.
A team of surgeons led by surgical gastroenterologist and director at GEM Hospital P.
Senthilnathan extracted the calculi with zero abdominal scars or stitches.
The patient was discharged just four days after the surgery.
Speaking to presspersons on Wednesday, he said that in chronic calcific pancreatitis, stones accumulate in the central duct and cause severe blockages, excruciating pain, and secondary diabetes.
“If left untreated, chronic inflammation can even increase the risk of pancreatic cancer.

As these stones sit dangerously close to major blood vessels, they must be extracted without fracturing or damaging the surrounding tissue, which is why such cases are almost universally managed through traditional open surgery, Dr. Senthilnathan added.

items.title: Look past grey market hype, focus on fundamentals when applying for IPOs
points: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has asked intermediaries and other market participants to stop publishing or circulating grey market premiums (GMPs) for upcoming initial public offerings (IPOs).
In its November 23, 2026, advisory, Sebi said the quotes are unofficial and unverified, and are derived from unregulated trades.
“Sebi’s concern is that GMP creates an illusion of price discovery where none actually exists.
Investors may mistake speculative market sentiment for a credible indication of the listing price,” says Pranav Haldea, managing director, PRIME Database Group.
Investors should understand the risks of grey market deals and of relying on GMPs to invest in IPOs for listing gains.
Without an allotment, the deal usually falls through,” says Eshaan Lazarus, founder and chief executive officer (CEO), 021 Trade.
“Smaller IPOs are more vulnerable because even relatively small trades can influence sentiment,” says Harsh Vira, founder and CEO, FinPro Wealth.
Skyways Air Services, for instance, had a GMP of 23 per cent, yet listed 10 per cent below its ₹138 issue price.

items.title: Transpetro carries out Suape’s first B30 bunkering
points: Petrobras’ shipping and logistics subsidiary Transpetro carried out the first B30 bunkering operation at Brazil’s Port of Suape on 22 November.
Transpetro supplied 520 mt of B30 to the crude oil tanker Castro Alves, which is part of its own fleet.
The blend comprised 30% biofuel and 70% VLSFO, and was delivered by barge at the port’s Liquid Bulk Pier 3B.
The operation makes Suape the second Brazilian port to join Petrobras’ Green Route project, which aims to expand the company’s bio-bunkering operations in Brazil.

Suape has also become the only port in the country’s North and Northeast regions to supply biofuel bunker blends, according to Armando Monteiro Bisneto, director-president of the Suape Port and Industrial Complex.
Petrobras plans to introduce biofuel bunkering at the ports of Rio Grande, Santos and São Sebastião through 2026 and 2027.
Ahead of the first delivery, the tanker Queen of Doria delivered blending components to Suape on 11 November, sufficient to produce up to 8,000 mt of B30.

items.title: Houthis threaten Saudi ports amid Yemen conflict escalation
points: Yemen’s Houthi movement warned Wednesday that the Saudi port of Jeddah and all other Saudi ports along the Red Sea coast would be targeted if Saudi Arabia moved to attack the Yemeni port of Hodeidah.
Houthi spokesperson Yahya Saree issued a statement urging port employees, workers, and nearby residents to evacuate immediately.
Following the Houthi warning, the Saudi-led coalition said it struck operational capabilities at Hodeidah and destroyed several targets in the Yemeni governorates of Saada and Amran.
The exchange follows a Houthi drone strike Tuesday on the tallest tower in Riyadh, which Saudi authorities said injured at least 11 people.
The Saudi-led coalition vowed a firm response to that attack.
Hodeidah is the main entry point for food and essential supplies into Houthi-controlled northern Yemen.
Clashes between the two sides have intensified since September, when the Houthis advanced toward the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a key shipping passage at the southern entrance to the Red Sea.

items.title: PSA Vietnam And Lach Huyen International Logistics & Industrial Park Break Ground For New Container Terminal In Hai Phong
points: PSA Vietnam (PSA) and Lach Huyen International Logistics & Industrial Park (LHF) marked the groundbreaking of their new container terminal at Lach Huyen, Hai Phong, North Vietnam on 23 November 2026.
With an annual handling capacity of 4.7 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs), the terminal will strengthen North Vietnam’s port infrastructure and connectivity to global markets.

Operating as Haiphong Xuan Cau PSA International Container Terminal (HXPICT), the terminal combines PSA’s port management expertise and global network with LHF’s industrial park and hinterland assets.
Together, this forms an integrated ecosystem that connects North Vietnam’s hinterland with the terminal and PSA’s global network.

Nelson Quek, Regional CEO, Southeast Asia, PSA International, said, “The development of HXPICT is an important milestone in advancing PSA’s Node to Network strategy, which seeks to connect ports and supply chain hubs into an integrated global network.
This collaboration strengthens PSA’s presence in North Vietnam and expands our network across key markets and trade routes, enabling us to better connect regional markets with global trade flows.

items.title: Imported iron ore margins increased on firmer port spot prices – Shanghai Metals Market (SMM)
points: The average imported iron ore margin rose from -8.78 yuan/mt to -4.30 yuan/mt.
The increase was mainly driven by higher port spot prices.
On the supply side, domestic ore concentrators in the Tangshan area have made no clear progress in resuming production.
Iron ore concentrate supply remained tight, and local prices were largely stable.

On the demand side, SMM data showed hot metal output lost to blast furnace maintenance was 1.8182 million mt in the week ended November 20, down 6,400 mt week-on-week, with maintenance largely unchanged.
Most mills in Tangshan were operating normally, and environmental curbs had a limited impact on blast furnaces.
Iron ore prices are likely to stay range-bound with a firmer bias in the short term, but gains are expected to be limited.
The market will watch the pace of mill winter restocking and changes in port inventories.

items.title: Durable goods orders rise less than expected, signaling economic caution
points: In a closely watched economic indicator, the latest data on durable goods orders has revealed a modest increase, but one that falls short of market expectations.
The actual rise in durable goods orders was reported at 0.2%, a figure that significantly underperformed against the forecasted 0.7%.
This development has raised questions about the strength and resilience of the manufacturing sector, a key component of the broader economy.
Durable goods orders, which track the total value of new orders placed with manufacturers for long-lasting items such as vehicles, appliances, and aircraft, are a vital barometer of economic health.
The latest numbers suggest a slowdown when compared to the previous month’s robust growth of 2.0%, indicating a potential cooling in demand for these high-value items.

A higher-than-expected reading typically signals economic strength and can be bullish for the U.S. dollar, while a lower reading, as observed, tends to have the opposite effect, potentially weighing on the currency.

items.title: U.S. Initial Jobless Claims Drop, Beating Forecasts
points: In a significant development for the U.S. labor market, the latest figures for initial jobless claims have been released, showing a notable decline.
The actual number of individuals filing for unemployment insurance for the first time came in at 189,000.
This figure represents a substantial drop from the forecasted 201,000 claims, indicating a stronger-than-expected labor market.
The decline in initial jobless claims also marks an improvement compared to the previous week’s figure of 202,000.
This trend suggests a continued strengthening of the employment sector, as fewer individuals seek unemployment benefits for the first time.
The initial jobless claims report is one of the earliest indicators of the health of the U.S. economy, providing insight into potential changes in employment trends.
The decline in claims may suggest that employers are holding onto workers despite broader economic uncertainties, which could translate into sustained consumer spending and economic growth.

items.title: U.S. drops business deal plan as Russia shows little interest – report
points: The Trump administration has set aside plans to use business deals as an incentive for Russia to end the war in Ukraine, after Moscow showed little interest in proposed energy and aviation ventures, the Financial Times reported Wednesday.

Trump’s envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner informed European officials that corporate partnerships were no longer a central part of the U.S. approach to Russia, according to five officials briefed on the shift in strategy, the report said.
Kushner, who has been working to broker a truce between Russia and Ukraine, had floated ideas including U.S. investment in Russian oil projects and titanium production ventures.

Top Russian and U.S. officials, including Kushner, also held talks about bringing a U.S. investor into the Nord Stream pipelines, which delivered gas to Germany before Russia invaded Ukraine, according to a report published in October.
Russian officials initially responded positively to the U.S. proposals, but their interest has since cooled.

items.title: US may cap India tariff at 17% if trade deal is reached
points: The United States could limit tariffs on Indian imports to 17% if the two countries reach a trade agreement, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said Wednesday.
Without a deal, tariffs on Indian goods would rise to 25%, he added.
The comments came as the Trump administration proposed new levies on 14 trading partners, citing what it describes as structural excess industrial capacity.
Washington listed several reasons for targeting India, including its industrial expansion policies, inadequate labor protections, financial repression, and barriers to market access.
The US also cited India’s failure to address global excess capacity, including through imports and foreign investment from non-market economies.
The US said these practices harm American producers, exports, jobs, and investment.
New Delhi and Washington agreed to a trade framework in February, which reduced the punitive tariff on most Indian goods to 18% from 50%.
That earlier tariff had been imposed in August 2025 after a previous round of trade talks broke down.

items.title: Red Sea and Indian Ocean Nations Advance Plans for Combined Maritime Security Force
points: Photo courtesy EUNAVFOR Countries bordering the Red Sea and Western Indian Ocean are moving toward establishing a combined maritime task force to combat piracy, strengthen regional security and protect commercial shipping across some of the world’s most…

The International Maritime Organization (IMO) announced that signatories to the Djibouti Code of Conduct and its Jeddah Amendment have adopted a new Regional Maritime Security Strategy and agreed to advance plans for a Combined Maritime Task Force (CMTF).
The agreement was reached during a high-level meeting held November 11–13 in Antananarivo, Madagascar.
The broader security strategy covers the Western Indian Ocean, Gulf of Aden and Red Sea.

Preparatory work began in Saudi Arabia in November 2024, with government representatives, navies, coast guards and maritime law enforcement agencies subsequently meeting in Mombasa, Kenya, earlier this month to finalize the framework.
Originally adopted in 2009 in response to Somali piracy, the Djibouti Code of Conduct was expanded in 2017 through the Jeddah Amendment to address a wider range of maritime security threats.

items.title: Hollow Knight Silksong’s Sea of Sorrow DLC Could Finally Get a Release Date This Friday
points: It’s been almost a year since Team Cherry announced the Hollow Knight Silksong Sea of Sorrow DLC, and fans have been eagerly waiting for more information ever since.
The wait is finally coming to an end, as the developers have announced a special livestream for this Friday, featuring new details about the upcoming expansion alongside several other announcements.
Dubbed Cherry Time, the special presentation is scheduled to take place on November 27, 2026, at 7 AM PT (10 AM ET / 3 PM GMT).
The livestream’s description promises “a bunch of exciting announcements” alongside an update on Hollow Knight Silksong’s Sea of Sorrow DLC.
With the expansion still scheduled for a 2026 release, we may finally get a release date during Friday’s livestream.
First announced in December 2025, Sea of Sorrow is a nautical-themed expansion that will continue Hornet’s adventures.
The DLC will introduce new areas to explore, tools to get your hands on, and add to the already extensive roster of bosses in Hollow Knight Silksong.

items.title: 'What Of 1984?' Sukhbir Badal After Congress Invokes Akal Takht Order Barring Ties With RSS
points: Turning the renewed alliance into a question of religious accountability, Channi has asked whether the Akali Dal, which has traditionally projected itself as a representative of Sikh interests, can enter an alliance with the BJP while continuing to abide…
Invoking the hukamnama dated July 2004, Channi said it directed the Sikh community and its leaders not to maintain ties with the RSS, the ideological mentor of the BJP.
"There is a hukamnama, a directive from Sri Akal Takht Sahib, issued on 23 July 2004, which mandates that the Sikh community must not maintain any ties with the RSS.

The 2004 Akal Takht directive was issued amid concerns over the activities of the RSS and its Sikh wing, Rashtriya Sikh Sangat, particularly their interpretation and projection of Sikh history and identity.
Sukhbir Singh Badal, however, refused to accept the challenge and turned the attack back on the Congress, invoking one of the most painful chapters in Sikh history - Operation Blue Star.

items.title: 'Children not toys for parents': SC sets aside Madras HC order granting custody to father
points: The Supreme Court on Wednesday set aside a Madras high court order awarding the custody of two boys to only their father, observing that children are neither the property nor toys of their parents.

A bench of Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh noted that the welfare of the child takes precedence over the legal rights of parents in a custody battle, and that the welfare of the children is best served by allowing them to stay with…

"The rule that a father should get custody of a child is always subject to exceptions and not universally applicable," the court said, noting that the boys expressed their inclination to stay with their mother and were unwilling to reside with their father.
According to LiveLaw, the matter relates to a Christian couple who got married in 2009 and divorced in 2014.
The woman obtained a decree of divorce alleging cruelty and sought custody of the children.

items.title: Ganga Water Treaty About To Lapse, Dhaka Makes Tough Demand From India
points: The Ganga Water Treaty between India and Bangladesh is likely to lapse as Bangladesh remains adamant on a guarantee clause in the treaty before it is renewed.
But even if the treaty lapses, Bangladesh does not have to worry too much about sharing of Ganga waters.
The foreign ministry said India is not going beyond the established bilateral mechanisms when it comes to talks on the Ganga Water Treaty.

"The expiry of the 1996 Ganga Water Treaty would technically remove the existing treaty-based framework for sharing and monitoring the waters of the Ganga at Farakka, but it in no way means that India acquires an unrestricted or unilateral prerogative over…

Under its existing water-sharing formula, the Ganga Water Treaty of 1996 signed between India and Bangladesh dictates that water is allocated every 10 days based on the flow recorded at Farakka point.

items.title: Italy Rebukes Ukraine Over Attacks on Russian Ships in Libya
points: Finnish Border Guard's handout photo of the Russian cargo ship Sparta II as the extinguishing of the fire continues in the Gulf of Finland November 22, 2026.

Finnish Border Guard/Handout via REUTERS ROME, Nov 25 (Reuters) – Italy has told Ukraine it was wrong to attack Russian ships in Libyan waters and warned Kyiv not to spread the war to new areas, Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani told Corriere della Sera…
“It was a mistake to violate Libya’s sovereignty,” Tajani said, adding that Rome had received no advance warning of the Ukrainian operations.
“Italy was absolutely unaware of Kyiv’s intentions to strike in Libyan territorial waters, even inside a port,” said the minister, who is head of the coalition Forza Italia party.

items.title: SEBI simplifies KYC norms, streamlines investor onboarding
points: Under the revised framework, investors will no longer be required to furnish common supplementary KYC details separately to each intermediary, as the information will be maintained centrally in the KRA system.
The move is aimed at reducing paperwork, streamlining account opening and improving the portability of KYC records across market intermediaries.
“It will avoid duplication in the submission of KYC records,” said Akshaya Bhansali, Managing Partner at Mindspright Legal.
“The process will become more centralised as all information will be available with KRAs.
SEBI has also allowed intermediaries to update client records using information available with KRAs and the Central KYC Records Registry (CKYCRR), subject to client confirmation.

The regulator has also eased compliance requirements for resident Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) cardholders and foreign nationals by making overseas address proof optional, provided they furnish a verified Indian address.
Further, several of the onboarding simplification measures will also apply to individual Persons Resident Outside India (PROI) from FATF-compliant countries.
The revised framework will come into force on December 24, 2026..

items.title: Indian investment in foreign capital hit $2 billion in H1FY27
points: Indian investments in global capital markets crossed $2 billion in the first half of FY27, according to outward remittance data in the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) September 2026 bulletin.

points: A speeding truck rammed college students waiting for a bus at the stop on a busy road in Pune on Wednesday, killing three and injuring six others.
The accident happened near Garwa Hotel in Pune's Bopdev Ghat at 1.34 pm.
CCTV footage shows the truck skidding off the road as it seemingly loses control and rams into college students standing at a bus stop on the side of the road.
As the truck approaches, the students are seen running away to save themselves, but some unfortunately got caught in the chaos and were run over by the big vehicle.
After hitting the students, the truck kept moving and left the scene.

items.title: Surat doctor gets two-year jail term for negligence in treatment of composer Ismail Darbar’s mother
points: A Surat court on Wednesday sentenced a doctor to two years of simple imprisonment for causing grievous injuries to the mother of Bollywood music composer Ismail Darbar through medical negligence during her treatment at a private hospital in 2009.
The court also imposed a fine of ₹1,000.

In a 95-page judgment, Judicial Magistrate First Class Pooja Surana convicted Dr Pareshkumar Bhajiyawala under Section 338 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), which deals with causing grievous hurt through an act that endangers human life or personal safety.
It also granted him bail of ₹15,000 during the appeal period.

items.title: US Proposes 25% Tariff On India. It Could Come Down With Trade Deal
points: The US on Wednesday proposed 25 per cent tariffs on Indian goods in the absence of a trade deal, citing excess industrial capacity, sustained market access barriers and inadequate labour protection that harm American companies.
The US Trade Representative (USTR) said the tariffs on India would amount to 17 per cent if it agrees to a trade deal with America.
The fresh tariff proposal follows Section 301 investigations launched by the USTR in March targeting 16 economic jurisdictions.
The USTR proposed tariffs of up to 20 per cent to 35 per cent on other targeted economies, though lower rates apply to trading partners with deals in place.
The EU, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and Switzerland face 15 per cent tariff rates, inclusive of standard import duties.
Vietnam would face tariffs of 20 per cent if the trade deal is finalised.

The investigation began last March, after the Supreme Court overturned the indiscriminate trade levies imposed by the Trump administration invoking the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA).

items.title: Royal Enfield Offers Free 10-Year Warranty In UK: Why India Could Be Next!
points: Royal Enfield is offering customers in the United Kingdom warranty protection for up to 10 years or 70,000 miles, whichever comes first.
The scheme started on 20 November 2026 and applies to eligible new as well as existing motorcycles.
That sounds like a major jump in confidence for a brand that builds many of its motorcycles in Chennai.
However, there is an important condition: owners must keep servicing their bikes through the authorised Royal Enfield network to extend the cover.
It is not a blanket 10-year warranty handed over on the day a bike is purchased, and it does not mean every repair over the next decade is free.
The 70,000-mile ceiling works out to roughly 1.13 lakh kilometres.
The company specifically excludes older UCE models and the 411cc Himalayan and Scram 411.
In India, Royal Enfield continues to offer a standard warranty of three years or 30,000 km on its current range, with an optional extension that can take total cover to five years or 50,000 km.

items.title: Government extends free travel for Chakra series gallantry awardees in all trains including Vande Bharat
points: The government has extended the complimentary train travel facility for recipients of Chakra series gallantry awards to all trains, including Vande Bharat, without changing their existing entitlements, officials said on Wednesday.

"Honouring valour, in a significant welfare initiative, the Ministry of Railways, in consultation with the Ministry of Defence, has enhanced the complimentary train travel facility for Chakra Series Awardees," it said.
"The facility now extends to all trains, including Vande Bharat, without any change in their existing entitlements," it added.
The initiative reflects a "shared commitment" to honouring the courage, sacrifice and service of the country's "yoddhas" and recognising their invaluable contribution to the nation, the Army said.
The first three gallantry awards instituted by the government after Independence were the Param Vir Chakra, Maha Vir Chakra and Vir Chakra.
They were instituted on January 26, 1950, with retrospective effect from August 15, 1947, according to the official website of gallantry awards.

items.title: Justice Vikram Nath applauds Justice Kaul’s candour amid debate over memoir

points: Meta officials on Tuesday met Congress leaders in Delhi and raised concerns about its employees and offices being targeted across India, people aware of the matter said.

The meeting follows nearly a week of protests by the Congress’s youth wing — Indian Youth Congress (IYC) — outside the company’s offices over allegations of restrictions on accounts and posts of their leaders critical of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

To be sure, the company in its latest transparency report disclosed a massive spike in content takedowns in India -- from 70,000 in 2025 to over 5 million in just the first six months of 2026 on government takedown orders.
Congress’s social media and digital platforms department chairperson Supriya Shrinate represented her party at the meeting.

items.title: CBI arrests proclaimed offender Kuldeep Kapoor in 2017 case of sending illegal workers to China
points: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has apprehended a proclaimed offender (PO), Kuldeep Kapoor, who is involved in a case related to the alleged trafficking of workers to China, the agency said on Wednesday.
The accused was taken into custody on Wednesday at Binauli Road in Baraut, Uttar Pradesh.

The federal agency had registered a case in July 2017 against Roshan Fernando, Kuldeep Kapoor and others, based on a complaint that they “fraudulently and dishonestly lured a lady with assurance of getting a Nepalese woman employment in China”.
“Both the accused persons were paid ₹1 lakh in instalments by the victim.

The statement came two days after Das was stopped at Delhi airport from flying to London for a speaking event where he, as a spokesperson of the activist group CJP, was to speak on the recent protests against the Narendra Modi government.

items.title: 2026 Toyota Innova HyCross Facelift: Photo Gallery
points: Toyota officially launched the much-awaited Hycross MPV in the Indian market today.
The MPV has been launched at an attractive introductory price of Rs 19.59 lakh for the regular petrol variant and Rs 19.99 lakh (ex-showroom) for the flex-fuel strong hybrid variant.
Compared to the outgoing version, Toyota has made a few changes to the MPV, and here we have an image gallery of the new Hycross explaining those changes.
The Innova Hycross also gets new double-stacked LED DRLs, along with tweaked projector headlamps and crystal LED fog lamps.

The Toyota Innova Hycross comes with a 360-degree camera and dual-zone climate control too.

items.title: Assam CM lays foundation for Northeast’s first ₹50-crore defence manufacturing unit at Tulsibari in Rangia
points: Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Wednesday laid the foundation stone for a defence equipment manufacturing facility being set up at Tulsibari in Rangia.
A Mumbai-based company, Speed4 Defence Systems Private Limited, will initially invest around ₹50 crore to establish the facility on approximately 14 acres of land.
Production is targeted to commence by January 2028.

Once fully operational, the facility will have the capacity to manufacture around 5,000 prefabricated rapidly deployable structures, 300 underground bunkers and protective structures, 100 counter-drone systems and 1,500 drones annually.

“As part of this initiative, the government would amend the Assam Aerospace and Defence Manufacturing Policy, 2025, to make the state more attractive to defence equipment manufacturing companies,” he added.

Sarma said that no defence manufacturing industry had so far been established in Assam or the Northeast and that the facility being set up in Tulsibari would be the first such manufacturing facility in the region.

items.title: Gujarat Teen Dies After Collapsing During Football Game In School
points: A 15-year-old student of Class 9 died on Wednesday after collapsing during a football match at Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya in Balasinor, Mahisagar district in Gujarat.
The boy, identified as Utsav Mehra, fell ill on the school campus and was rushed to a nearby hospital for emergency medical care, where doctors declared him dead.
Utsav was reportedly playing football with other students on school premises when he suddenly started feeling unwell and fell on the ground.
Despite being rushed to hospital for treatment, he could not make it, leaving his classmates, teachers, and family struck by the tragedy.
Doctors examining the case suspect a silent heart attack as the preliminary cause of death, though officials said that the exact cause is yet to be confirmed.
The boy's body was sent to the Balasinor government hospital for a post-mortem examination.
Medical and laboratory results from the collected samples are awaited to establish the exact cause of death.

items.title: Nvidia stock loses momentum after Huang's return as CEO, down another 9%; why are investors dumping AI stocks again?
points: Shares of Nvidia slipped another 9% in Wednesday's opening bell on New York, 25 November, to the day's low of $141 apiece, giving up much of Monday's gains following the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO.
Wednesday's decline came on the back of a 6% drop in the previous session, taking the stock's cumulative two-day decline to 14.5% from Monday's levels, based on the day's low.

The report comes as markets are fully pricing in a quarter-percentage-point interest rate hike when the Fed meets on December 8-9.

items.title: Congress wins Bharatpur zila pramukh poll in CM Bhajan Lal Sharma’s home district
points: Days after sweeping the Rajasthan panchayat polls, the Congress on Wednesday won the zila pramukh election in Bharatpur, the home district of Chief Minister Bhajanlal Sharma, defeating the BJP in a closely watched contest amid allegations of horse-trading…
Congress candidate Renu Wala secured 17 votes against 14 by BJP's Pooja Jatav, ensuring that the district Panchayati Raj body remained under the party's control.

The contest assumed political significance as the BJP was seeking to secure control of the zila parishad in the chief minister's home district despite the Congress scoring a decisive victory in the recent local body polls.
A zila parishad is the top district-level body of the three-tier Panchayati Raj system, whose members are directly elected by voters from wards across the district.
The elected members choose a zila pramukh or the head of the zila parishad from among themselves.

items.title: US deported 1,700 Indians in 2026 so far, India says it opposes illegal immigration
points: The US has deported 1,700 Indian nationals since the start of this year, and the Indian side is firmly opposed to illegal immigration and is cooperating with American authorities on all matters related to migration and mobility, the external affairs…

“Since the beginning of this year, we’ve had 1,700 Indian nationals deported from [the US],” external affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said in response to a question on the matter at a regular media briefing.
“We have ongoing cooperation with the US on migration and mobility and India is firmly against illegal immigration.
These 1,700 Indians were deported “for one reason or the other”, he said without going into details.
The external affairs ministry had said in July that the US had deported more than 4,800 Indian nationals since 2025.
The US administration stepped up the deportation of illegal migrants from across the world as part of a crackdown that began soon after President Donald Trump took office last year.

items.title: RBI raises share of domestically held gold reserves, data shows
points: As of September, the Reserve Bank of India has expanded its domestic gold reserves to 880.52 metric tonnes.
This figure comprises 740.13 metric tonnes held in the country and 140.39 metric tonnes stored internationally.
However, the proportion of gold within the overall reserves has declined to 14.38%.
Currently, India's total foreign exchange reserves stand at $705.3 billion, predominantly invested in foreign government securities.

items.title: The Ignis Is Back, And You'll Be Surprised At How It Looks Now!
points: The Maruti Suzuki Ignis quietly disappeared from showrooms earlier this year.
The new Ignis was revealed globally on 25 November 2026 and is based on Suzuki's e SKY electric kei car, which went on sale in Japan on 16 November.
The Ignis name will be used for the international version, with sales scheduled to begin in Europe and other markets from summer 2027.
At 3,570 mm long, 1,565 mm wide and 1,635 mm tall, the new Ignis is 130 mm shorter and 125 mm narrower than the petrol Ignis sold here, but 40 mm taller.
A front-mounted electric motor produces 91 PS and 133 Nm, and it draws power from a 26 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery.
The related Japan-market e SKY is rated at 310 km under Japan's WLTC test cycle, but that number should not be treated as the confirmed range of the international Ignis.
For India, the name brings back memories of the Ignis launched through Nexa in January 2017.

items.title: India-China military commanders’ talks focus on border management, outstanding issues along LAC
points: The discussions, believed to have lasted more than a week, were the second round of such talks in the Arunachal Pradesh sector since September.
They were held following reports of aggressive posturing by Chinese troops along the Line of Actual Control (LAC), especially in the Upper Subansiri region.

Discussions between the two sides focused on improving border management, as also addressing outstanding issues along the LAC,” external affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal told a regular media briefing when he was asked about the talks.

Lt Gen Girish Kalia, General Officer Commanding of the Indian Army’s 3 Corps based near Dimapur in Nagaland, led the Indian side at the talks held in the second week of November, while the Chinese side was headed by his counterpart.
In September, Kalia and a Chinese military commander held flag talks in two sessions on either side of the LAC in the Arunachal Pradesh sector.

items.title: Assam to get two more advanced data centres as govt signs MoU with Bharti Airtel
points: The Assam government and Bharti Airtel Limited on Wednesday signed an agreement to set up two data centres in Jorhat and Silchar, involving a combined initial investment of ₹455 crore.
The projects, with a proposed capacity of 25 MW, are expected to generate around 164 direct jobs, chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said.

The proposed 10 MW data centre in Jorhat will be built on around four acres of land at an initial investment of ₹200 crore.
The 15 MW facility in Silchar will come up on approximately five acres, with an initial investment of ₹255 crore, Sarma said.

The two projects, with a combined investment of ₹455 crore, are expected to create around 164 direct jobs, besides generating indirect employment in construction, engineering, security, maintenance and other allied sectors.

items.title: PhonePe revives IPO plans, eyes $12-15 billion valuation; filing likely in a fortnight
points: Walmart-owned PhonePe has revived its initial public offering (IPO) plans and is targeting a stock market debut in the fourth quarter of FY27, banking sources said.
The digital payments major is likely to file an updated draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) within the next fortnight and is seeking a valuation of $12-15 billion.
The proposed public issue is expected to raise around ₹12,000 crore ($1.3 billion) through a pure offer for sale (OFS), under which existing shareholders will dilute their stakes, the sources said.
Its topline has been growing at around 40 per cent, while its credit business has expanded by nearly 100 per cent year-on-year, bankers said.
For FY26, PhonePe reported an 11 per cent increase in consolidated revenue to ₹7,920 crore, against ₹7,115 crore in FY25.
However, its consolidated net loss widened 62 per cent to ₹2,792 crore (₹1,727 crore).
PhonePe is India’s largest digital payments platform, with more than 45 per cent share of UPI transactions.

points: About 248,000 new companies were added in FY26, and paid-up capital stood at ₹68.6 lakh crore.

items.title: Baroda BNP Paribas Mutual Fund targets ₹1.50 lakh crore AUM in 5 years
points: Baroda BNP Paribas Mutual Fund targets to increase its asset under management to ₹1.50 lakh crore in five years from ₹60,000 crore by widening investors outreach and launching products that are best suited for investors.
Besides the reach through Bank of Baroda branches, the fund house plans to double its branch count to 50 in three years and work along with distributors to increase the investors count.
Madhu Nair, CEO, Baroda BNP Paribas MF said the potential for growth in mutual fund space is immense but the intention is to provide the investment product to investors.
The fund house’s AUM has grown from ₹54,000 crore to ₹60,000 crore with the equity asset of ₹30,000 crore and hybrid of ₹35,000 crore, he said.
Bank of Baroda has 18 crore customers and Baroda BNP Paribas MF investors base is about 7 lakh which reflects the growth potential of this business, he added.

items.title: SEBI retains BSE 200, Nifty CPSE in Significant Indices list despite threshold miss
points: In a circular, the market regulator said the overall list of Significant Indices remains unchanged following its half-yearly review for the six months ended June 30.
However, the two indices — BSE 200 and Nifty CPSE — did not satisfy the eligibility threshold of ₹20,000 crore in daily average cumulative AUM during the review period.
SEBI said the BSE 200 and Nifty CPSE would continue to remain on the list under the provisions of its May 5 circular, which provides for their retention despite not meeting the prescribed threshold.

items.title: Hyundai Does A Mahindra: Gifts Paralympian Sheetal Devi Bayon SUV
points: Hyundai has gifted a new Bayon SUV to para-archer Sheetal Devi, who returned from the 2026 Asian Para Games with two gold medals and a silver.

items.title: ‘No power wants India to rise’: Mohan Bhagwat says global powers want to retain dominance
points: Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat on Wednesday said that no power in the world wants India to rise, arguing that global powers seek to establish control over others, while India's approach is based on helping everyone.
Speaking about the approach adopted by powerful nations, Bhagwat said, "No power in the world wants India to rise.
What have these powers used their strength for?
But if Bharat becomes powerful, all these shops will shut down because Bharat helps everyone," he added.

Addressing the 'Maru Ninad-2026' Ghosh Shivir organised by the RSS Jodhpur Prant at Rajaram Ashram in Shikarpura, Bhagwat remarked that while India is moving in the right direction today, certain global forces do not want the nation to become great.

items.title: Ghaziabad woman held captive, sexually assaulted inside Meerut hotel; accused arrested
points: A 24-year-old woman from Ghaziabad was allegedly held captive and sexually assaulted at a hotel in Meerut's Abu Lane for two days, according to police.
Salman, was arrested after a brief encounter with police on Wednesday, and the hotel was sealed.

items.title: Electric Two-Wheelers: TVS Motors Leads With 26% Marketshare, Ola Electric Crashes To 6.7%

items.title: LG Electronics shares to be in focus as promoter to sell 2% stake to meet public float norms; check details
points: LG Electronics, a leading single-brand home appliances player, is likely to be on investors' radar in Thursday's trade, as its promoter, LG Electronics Inc. , is set to offload a 2% stake in the company through a block deal.
The floor price has been set at ₹1,709.30 per share, according to the company's filing.
The offer involves the sale of up to 13.58 million shares, worth up to ₹2,320.5 crore.
The proposed stake sale is part of the promoter's efforts to meet the minimum public shareholding (MPS) requirements.

MPS is a regulatory requirement in India that mandates listed companies to maintain a minimum percentage of their total equity share capital in the hands of non-promoter public shareholders, typically 25%.

items.title: Most Large Fuel Tankers Now Ship ‘Dirty’ Crude, Upending Trading
points: Nov 25, 2026 (Bloomberg) –A record three-quarters of the global fleet of large tankers designed to transport oil products are tapping higher earnings to ship crude, keeping the cost to move fuels elevated.
Less than a quarter of the world’s 542 long-range 2, or LR2, tankers are currently transporting “clean” cargoes such as jet fuel, naphtha and diesel as of this week, according to Signal Ocean data.
The shift in use of the LR2 fleet comes as crude flows recover through the Strait of Hormuz.

Benchmark earnings for very-large crude carriers have soared, in turn enabling smaller-sized tankers — including Aframaxes, which are the crude-focused equivalent of LR2s, able to hold about 750,000 barrels — to command far higher fees.

Even though the LR2 fleet has grown 12% since January last year and clean-fuel shipments have fallen due to the US-Iran war, the increased switching to crude has helped put a floor underneath the fees they can command to carry oil products.

points: Icebreaker USCGC Healy’s damaged diesel engine will be inspected by a contractor to find out which of its parts can be saved after a major failure in July, as per the US Coast Guard.
A procurement notice issued on October 21 calls for a full inspection of the cutter’s number 2 main propulsion diesel engine, which is a Sulzer 12ZAV40S.
The work will be carried out at Coast Guard Base Seattle and includes checking wear on components and measuring clearances.
An optional item worth up to $100,000 has also been included for inspecting, repairing and requalifying the engine’s camshaft.
The Coast Guard intends to give the job to Chesapeake-based Defence Maritime Solutions in Virginia on a sole-source basis, and the inspection was planned for October 26 to 30.
As per Coast Guard documents, the number 2 main propulsion diesel generator suffered a catastrophic overspeed failure that also sparked a fire in the generator room.

items.title: US Navy Picks Raytheon To Develop Submarine-Launched Nuclear Cruise Missile SLCM-N
points: Nuclear-Armed Sea-Launched Cruise Missile (SLCM-N) of the US Navy has moved from early concept work into development after Raytheon received a new agreement from the service.
The award was made under the Navy’s Other Transaction Authority to Raytheon, which is a business unit of RTX.
The SLCM-N is a nuclear cruise missile that is meant to restore a theatre-level nuclear option at sea lost after the nuclear Tomahawk (TLAM-N) was retired in 2013.
The Navy expects delivery in 2034, and the missile will use a new W80-5 warhead variant.
The Navy has awarded five prototype agreements worth about $743.6 million.
Its May shipbuilding plan envisions roughly 450 vessels by the early 2030s, pairing 299 crewed warships with 83 unmanned vessels and 68 auxiliary ships.
SLCM-N will be operated from Virginia-class attack submarines, giving the Navy a survivable regional nuclear option as autonomous craft take on more of the fleet’s scouting, strike and sensing work.
References: Raytheon, Defence Industry Europe, Yahoo Finance

items.title: Ukraine Says Drone Strike That Sank Russian Corvette Merkury In Libya Was Self-Defence
points: Ukraine has defended its drone attack that sank the Russian corvette Merkury in Libya’s eastern port of Benghazi as a lawful act of self-defence.
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha stated on November 24, 2026, that the weekend strike on the warship and a cargo ship in Libyan waters was covered by Article 51 of the United Nations Charter.
He argued that Russian naval vessels as well as cargo ships carrying military equipment were valid targets for Ukraine.
Libya’s Western-backed Government of National Unity (GNU) in Tripoli condemned the operation on Monday and warned that the country would not accept being drawn into the Russia-Ukraine war.
The Libyan National Army (LNA), which controls eastern Libya, confirmed that two of its personnel died from injuries suffered in the strike on Benghazi port.

The Russian corvette had stayed at Benghazi port for several days to refuel and resupply while escorting cargo ships that can carry military supplies to Russia, according to a think tank that tracks the war.

items.title: Toyota Innova Hycross Facelift E85 Flex Fuel Hybrid Launch Price Rs 19.99 L
points: Toyota has launched the Innova Hycross facelift in India, bringing a revised exterior, additional equipment and a flex-fuel strong-hybrid powertrain.
The biggest development is compatibility with ethanol-petrol blends ranging from E20 to E85.
Toyota is presenting the updated powertrain under its Flex Hybrid Electric branding.
Toyota Innova Hycross facelift introductory prices start at Rs 19.59 lakh for the petrol GX variant.
Toyota has confirmed G, GX, VX and ZX variants for the Flex Hybrid Electric powertrain.
The E20–E85 compatible flex-fuel strong-hybrid range starts at Rs 19.99 lakh for G (comes with speed limiting function), followed by GX at Rs 23.99 lakh, VX at Rs 28.79 lakh and ZX at Rs 31.99 lakh.
The new Innova Hycross flex-fuel hybrid supports petrol blended with between 20% and 85% ethanol.
It is powered by the same 2.0-litre strong hybrid produced 186 hp of combined system output, while its petrol engine developed 191 Nm.

items.title: Indian Navy ships, helicopters deployed to search for 7 fishermen missing off Andhra coast: Officials
points: Indian Navy ships and helicopters have been deployed as the search continues for seven fishermen from Andhra Pradesh’s Kakinada district who went missing in the Bay of Bengal amid cyclonic conditions, officials said on Wednesday.
The fishermen were last sighted near Odisha’s Paradip Port on November 18.

Kakinada district collector M N Harendhira Prasad said the Indian Coast Guard and the Indian Navy had launched a joint search operation to trace the seven fishermen from Subbampeta village in Uppada mandal.
The missing fishermen have been identified as D Simhadri, the boat owner, Kodanda Rao, Gampala Prakash, Tirri Narayana, Korada Chinna, Merugu Narayana and Kandala Ramu.
According to officials, they reached Visakhapatnam harbour on November 11 and informed their families that they would venture further into the sea for fishing.

The district administration received information about the missing fishermen from their families on November 19, following which it alerted the Coast Guard and began coordinating with the concerned agencies to trace them, the collector said.

items.title: Shenzhen Energy makes $44m dry bulk newbuild move
points: Chinese power group Shenzhen Energy is moving ahead with the renewal of its dry bulk fleet, selecting CSSC Huangpu Wenchong Shipbuilding to build an 82,000 dwt kamsarmax in a deal worth RMB296m ($44.4m).

The Shenzhen-listed company’s shipping arm, Shenzhen Energy Transportation, has named the Guangzhou-based yard as the winning bidder for the vessel, which will replace its ageing 1997-built, 69,000 dwt panamax Jia Chang (pictured).
The award follows an investment decision in June, when Shenzhen Energy approved a budget of RMB309.68m ($46.5m) for the newbuilding as part of efforts to modernise its coal transportation fleet.
The vessel will be designed to run on conventional marine fuels, with provision for a future conversion to methanol propulsion.
According to the group’s earlier stock exchange disclosure, the project will be financed through RMB64m in internal funds, with the remainder covered by external financing.
Shenzhen Energy Transportation operates six panamax bulk carriers totalling around 450,000 dwt, transporting coal to the group’s power plants while also serving the international dry bulk market.

items.title: New Toyota Innova Hycross Facelift Launched In India At Rs 19.59 Lakh
points: Toyota has launched the Innova HyCross facelift in India, with prices starting at Rs 19.59 lakh (ex-showroom).
The Toyota Innova Hycross facelift comes to India with a petrol engine, a petrol hybrid powertrain and importantly, a flex fuel variant.
The strong hybrid flex fuel variant starts at Rs 19.99 lakh, ex-showroom - very close to the price of the base petrol variant.

The equipment array now has a 12.3-inch touchscreen infotainment system (new) , a 12.3-inch instrument cluster (new), Level 2 ADAS, ventilated seats, powered driver's seat, 9-speaker JBL premium audio, a panoramic sunroof, ottoman seats in the second row,…
Some of these were introduced in the recently-launched Indonesian-spec Kijang Innova Zenix.
The Innova HyCross facelift continues with two familiar powertrain options.
The first is a 2.0-litre naturally aspirated petrol engine that produces 173PS and 204Nm of torque.
It combines the petrol engine with an electric motor and a small battery pack, and delivers a combined output of 184PS.

items.title: Saurav Das was asked for clarification on place of birth, advised not to use passport for 7 days: MEA
points: The external affairs ministry on Wednesday said that a show-cause notice had been issued to Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convenor Saurav Das, asking him to explain discrepancies in his place of birth in his passport and advising him not to use the travel…
This came after Das moved the Delhi high court on Monday, alleging that he was stopped from travelling to London to deliver a lecture at Oxford Union.

External affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the Regional Passport Office (RPO) in Chennai issued a show-cause notice to Das on November 23, requesting a clarification within seven days regarding his place of birth.

"Based on reports that we received from the relevant law enforcement authorities, the Regional Passport Office (RPO) in Chennai issued a show-cause notice to Saurav Das on November 23, requesting a clarification within seven days regarding his place of birth.
The matter was mentioned before Acting Chief Justice Nitin Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma on Wednesday.

items.title: Military doctors carry out 412 free, sight-restoring surgeries at eye camp in Meerut
points: Armed Forces Medical Services (AFMS) doctors performed 412 free, sight-restoring surgeries at a surgical eye camp at Military Hospital, Meerut, under Operation Drishti, the defence ministry said on Wednesday.

The surgeries were performed by a team from Army Hospital (Research & Referral), led by Brigadier Sanjay Kumar Mishra, who is spearheading Operation Drishti, a series of large-scale surgical eye camps aimed at bringing advanced eye care to remote and…
The camp was organised under the aegis of Lucknow-based HQ Surya Command.

“The five-day camp, which concluded on November 25, brought a ‘new lease of light’ to people across the region, including 197 underprivileged civilians, who underwent surgeries for cataract, glaucoma, vitreo-retinal and pterygium.
One of the highlights was the successful surgeries of 60 mature cataract patients who were completely blind,” the defence ministry said in a statement.

items.title: SEBI explores AI sandbox, domestically governed model for securities market
points: FILE PHOTO: SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey says the regulator is exploring an AI sandbox and a domestically governed AI model for the securities market.

Addressing the Dhanam BFSI Summit 2026 in Kochi, Pandey said responsible innovation, stronger cybersecurity and effective governance would be critical as technology increasingly transforms financial services and capital markets.
“We are exploring an AI Sandbox to test applications in a controlled environment.
We are also examining a domestically governed AI model for the securities market to make secure and affordable AI tools more widely accessible,” he said.
Highlighting Sebi's use of artificial intelligence, Pandey said the regulator is deploying technology to strengthen market surveillance and investor protection.
"An alert is not a finding, and an algorithm cannot assume responsibility," he said, stressing the need for reliable data, effective oversight and sound risk management.
Pandey said the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is reviewing the framework for initial public offerings (IPOs) and SME IPOs to make public fundraising more accessible.

items.title: BSE, Eternal, Titan, SBI among 18 Nifty 50 stocks that rallied 10–43% in 2026; what's driving gains?
points: BSE, Eternal and Apollo Hospitals were among the 18 constituents of the Nifty 50 that surged between 12% and 43% in 2026 so far, as the tide finally turned in favour of Dalal Street bulls after they were pushed back amid bouts of market volatility.
Leading the rally was BSE, with a 43.42% surge, followed by Eternal, Apollo Hospitals and Adani Ports, which gained between 31% and 34%.

Other stocks in the pack included ICICI Bank, Adani Enterprises, Trent, SBI, Bajaj Auto, Titan, Kotak Mahindra Bank, Bajaj Finance, Eicher Motors, Tech Mahindra, IndiGo, JSW Steel, Grasim and Axis Bank.
All these stocks advanced in the range of 10% to 22%.
As major heavyweights joined the recovery rally, the Nifty 50 surged 12% in November and is on track to record its biggest monthly gain since April 2020.
The rally has also narrowed its year-to-date losses to just 1.19%.

items.title: Small-cap stock under ₹100 sets board meeting date to announce ₹648 crore fund raise | Record date, other details
points: Small-cap stock under ₹100: The board of directors of the pharma company Shukra Medtech Ltd has announced a board meeting date to announce the record date for the preferential issue to raise ₹648 crore.
The board meeting date has been fixed on 2 December 2026 to consider and approve a ₹60 crore fundraise through the preferential offer.

The Indian rupee strengthened to its highest level for the fiscal year against the dollar.

items.title: SEBI chief flags gap between market awareness and investor participation
points: FILE PHOTO: SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey speaks at the Dhanam BFSI Summit 2026 in Kochi, stressing transparency, investor protection and financial literacy.

Speaking at the Dhanam BFSI Summit 2026 in Kochi, Pandey stressed that financial inclusion must translate into financial empowerment, enabling investors to make decisions based on their financial goals and understanding of risks.
Citing SEBI’s 2025 Investor Survey, the chairman highlighted the gap between financial awareness and actual participation in the securities market.
“Around 63% of households knew of at least one securities-market product, but only 9.5% participated.
Even among investors, only 36% had moderate or high market knowledge,” he said.
The findings assume significance as India’s securities market now has more than 15 crore unique investors, while mutual funds manage assets worth around Rs 83 lakh crore.
The regulator is also expanding its investor awareness efforts through Project Jagrook, launched nationwide on October 5, 2026.

items.title: SEBI proposes up to 80% early payout for FPOs in commodity derivatives
points: SEBI has proposed an early payout facility allowing eligible Farmer Producer Organisations to receive up to 80 per cent of commodity derivatives sale proceeds before contract expiry.

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) on Wednesday proposed allowing Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) to receive up to 80 per cent of the value of their sale transactions on commodity derivatives exchanges up to 30 days before contract…

In a consultation paper titled ‘Early Pay Out (EPO) of funds for Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs)’, the market regulator proposed a framework under which eligible trading members could release funds to FPOs against agricultural commodities deposited in…

“A maximum of 80% of the value of the sale transaction of the derivatives contract executed on the exchange, may be released as early pay-out to the FPO clients,” SEBI said in the draft circular accompanying the consultation paper.
While these organisations can receive funds immediately upon executing trades in physical markets, commodity derivatives transactions involve a waiting period for the realisation of sale proceeds.

items.title: India wins Visitors’ Lion for best national pavilion at 61st Venice Art Biennale from among 100 participants
points: India won the Visitors’ Lion for the Best National Pavilion at the recently-concluded 61st Venice Art Biennale in Italy, from among a 100 national participants.
Chicago-born musician and artist Nick Cave won the Visitors' Lion for Best Participant.

The awards were based on "preferences expressed by the public through votes cast by visitors to the 61st International art exhibition," which ran from May 9 to November 22, the Venice Biennale management announced on November 25.
India wins the Best National Pavilion – Visitors’ Lion at the Venice Art Biennale, the Olympics of the art world.

The Union ministry of culture and tourism partnered with the Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre and Serendipity Arts to present India's national pavilion under the curatorial theme, "Geographies of Distance: Remembering Home".

In a statement released days before the Biennale was slated to open, the five-member jury refused to consider any national pavilion or artist "whose leaders are currently charged with crimes against humanity by the International Criminal Court", in an…

items.title: Bonny Gas Transport adds LNG carrier double in China
points: Nigeria LNG’s shipping arm Bonny Gas Transport (BGT) has returned to China’s Hudong-Zhonghua Shipbuilding for another two LNG carriers, expanding its fleet renewal programme at the Shanghai yard to five firm vessels.
The Nigerian owner has signed contracts on for a pair of 174,000 cu m newbuilds, with China Shipbuilding Trading also involved in the agreement.
The latest deal follows BGT’s earlier three-ship programme at the same yard, which was first reported in late 2025 and subsequently confirmed by Nigeria LNG in June this year.
Those vessels, also of 174,000 cu m capacity, are scheduled for delivery between the second and third quarters of 2029.
They will be chartered by Nigeria LNG and managed by NLNG Shipping and Marine Services.
The earlier three firm ships were estimated at $248m each.
The investment adds to BGT’s efforts to replace older tonnage supporting LNG exports from Nigeria’s Bonny Island complex.

items.title: Tamil Nadu TVK MLA summoned over sexual harassment complaint by district collector: Police
points: Tamil Nadu’s Kallakurichi police on Wednesday summoned Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) MLA C Arul Vignesh for questioning in connection with a sexual harassment complaint filed against him by a district collector, as a special team was constituted to…
A team comprising a senior officer from the Kallakurichi All Women Police Station and a constable visited Vignesh’s residence in T Ramaswamy Nagar on Wednesday morning to serve the summons.

The Kallakurichi All Women Police Station had registered a first information report (FIR) under various sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) after the district collector lodged a formal complaint alleging that the legislator had sent her obscene…
On November 24, while hearing the case, Madras High Court judge V Lakshminarayanan directed the state government to constitute a team to investigate the allegations.
Tiruppur superintendent of police Srishti Singh has been assigned to lead the investigation, under the supervision of inspector general of police (Administration) Kamini.

items.title: Toyota Hycross Facelift Final Production Version Revealed, LAUNCH Happening Now!
points: Toyota has finally revealed the production version of the much-awaited Toyota Innova HyCross facelift.
With time still left for the car to be on stage, here is what we know about the design of the new HyCross.
From the images that have surfaced, it is clear that the facelift has got a major cosmetic upgrade.
Slim metallic strips extend from the dark panel towards the headlamps.

However, minor changes can be spotted in the design of the rear bumper and detailing of the tail lamps.
The new Hycross is likely to borrow many of its features from the Kijang Innova Zenix sold in Indonesia.

If so, it will come with the likes of a 12.3-inch touchscreen infotainment system, Level 2 ADAS , a 7-inch TFT multi-information display, and panoramic sunroof, digital video recorder, panoramic view monitor and more.

items.title: HMD Rise 4G Tipped to Launch in India Soon; Could Arrive as the Rebranded HMD Arc 2
points: HMD Rise 4G will be launched soon in India, a tipster claims.

It is shown to feature a flat rear panel, with a pill-shaped camera module placed in the top-left corner.
The handset could be offered in at least a blue shade, similar to HMD Arc 2’s Dark Blue colour option.
Further, the power button and volume controls are expected to be placed on the right side of the rumoured HMD Rise 4G.
The camera module could be redesigned to reposition the LED flash between the camera cutouts, unlike the HMD Arc 2, which features an LED flash placed inside one of the camera cutouts.
The AI camera branding also appears at the back.
The poster features the tagline, “Rise With Every Shot”, along with the text, “Coming Soon”.

items.title: Indian aluminium body urges government to hike import duty to 10%, regulate scrap consignments
points: The Aluminium Association of India (AAI) has urged the Government to strengthen the industry’s value chain, improve the competitiveness of domestic manufacturers and support the growth of the sector.

In its pre-Budget memorandum, AAI has proposed increasing the basic customs d(BCD) on primary aluminium to 10 per cent, maintaining or increasing the duty on aluminium scrap with primary aluminium, and raising the duty on downstream product imports to 15…

It called for increasing import duties on aluminium scrap till mandatory quality controls allowing only those with over91 per cent aluminium content are in place, in line with the Government of India’s Aluminium Vision Document and global peers.
In its pre-Budget memorandum, AAI said this is crucial in view of aluminium demand being projected to rise from around 6 million tonnes in FY26 to 11.5 million tonnes by FY33.
The industry has indicated an investment pipeline of approximately ₹4 lakh crore to expand domestic capacity and meet this demand.

items.title: SEBI retains BSE 200, Nifty CPSE in significant indices list despite missing AUM threshold
points: The market regulator, in a circular, said the existing list of significant indices under the SEBI (Index Providers) Regulations, 2024, will remain unchanged following the half-yearly review.

Under SEBI’s circular dated May 5, 2026, a benchmark or index is considered significant if the daily average cumulative AUM tracking the benchmark or index across mutual fund schemes exceeds Rs 20,000 crore for each of the preceding six months, ending June…
During the latest review, the BSE 200 and Nifty CPSE indices did not meet the prescribed threshold.
However, SEBI retained both indices in accordance with the provisions of its earlier circular.
“However, these indices are being retained in the list in terms of Para 5 of the said circular,” SEBI said.
Accordingly, the BSE 200 and Nifty CPSE indices continue to retain their significant index status despite not meeting the threshold during the latest review period.
The circular is addressed to all index providers, stock exchanges, mutual funds, asset management companies and the Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI).

items.title: Global convulsions, courtesy AI stocks, creates a $385 billion winner — India
points: The NSE Nifty 50 soared 1.9% on Wednesday, while Asian equities slumped, tracking declines in US technology stocks as investors questioned whether lofty AI valuations and massive spending plans can be sustained.
The MSCI India index has added nearly $385 billion in value this month, as a market long shunned for its lack of AI plays emerges as a bright spot for global investors.
Stock benchmarks in India have rallied more than 12% in November, beating more than 90 major global equity indexes tracked by Bloomberg.
Global funds have poured nearly $14 billion into local equities in November, a monthly record, after withdrawing unprecedented sums earlier this year.
The currency rallied 0.7% to 92.23 per dollar on Wednesday, its strongest level since March 12.

items.title: Hong Kong shipowners hail shipping tax overhaul
points: The Hong Kong Shipowners Association (HKSOA) has welcomed a package of tax reforms aimed at attracting more shipping and commodity trading businesses to the city, including a new half-rate profits tax concession for physical commodity traders.

The measures, which returned to the Legislative Council for consideration on Wednesday, would reduce the profits tax rate on qualifying commodity trading activities from 16.5% to 8.25%, while expanding existing concessions for ship leasing, shipmanagement,…

The legislation also introduces an optional 15% tax rate for qualifying shipping companies and commodity traders covered by the OECD’s global minimum tax rules, allowing them to simplify compliance under the BEPS 2.0 framework.
The commodity trading concession is designed to bring more trading houses to Hong Kong and generate additional demand for local shipping services.

Under the proposed framework, eligible traders must meet minimum business turnover and local operating requirements, including conditions linking expenditure on maritime services to Hong Kong-based providers.

items.title: PhonePe revives IPO plans, targets $12-15 billion valuation in early 2027
points: PhonePe, which has over 650 million registered users, processed nearly 11.4 billion UPI transactions in India in October.

Indian fintech PhonePe has resumed preparations for its initial public offering and is targeting a listing in the first three months of next year at a valuation of $12 billion to $15 billion, a person directly aware of the discussions said.

The Walmart-backed company is expected to file its updated draft papers with India’s market regulator, the Securities and Exchange Board of India, within the next 30 to 45 days, the person said, requesting anonymity as talks are confidential.
The listing is set to be India’s biggest fintech debut since Paytm’s $2.5 billion float in 2021.

The issue will be an entirely secondary share sale to raise $1.2 billion to $1.5 billion, retaining the size outlined in PhonePe’s January draft prospectus, where majority owner Walmart said it would trim its stake by about 12%, and investors Tiger Global…

items.title: Fed policymakers at odds over causes of high inflation
points: US inflation is expected to increase again in October, with potential implications for Federal Reserve interest rate decisions.
Economists predict the Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index to reach 3.8% this month.
Analysts are divided regarding whether inflation is caused by demand or supply shocks stemming from recent policies.
Market forecasts suggest three more rate hikes, signaling ongoing concerns about rising prices.

items.title: Pak show Dar-e-Nijaat’s screenings cancelled in Bengaluru after backlash
points: Two private screenings of a Pakistani television serial named ‘Dar-e-Nijaat’ were cancelled in Bengaluru as organisers withdrew their plans after online backlash over the move.
The screenings of ‘Dar-e-Nijaat’ were to be held on November 28 and December 5 at two separate venues.
Both invitations specified Pakistani clothing as the dress code, a detail that became central to the objections raised on social media.
A representative of Sheesh Kebab confirmed that the November 28 programme had been called off but did not explain the decision.
The host of the December 5 screening said the event had been intended for family members and a small group of acquaintances.
The first gathering was planned by The Bloom Society Sisters' Club at Sheesh Kebab in Frazer Town in east Bengaluru.
The organisers had advertised a screening of two episodes, 34 and 35, followed by a Persian and Arabic dinner.
The second event, hosted by The Star Club at Mowie Private Theatre in Jayamahal Extension, was also billed as a private screening.

items.title: ‘Sincerely apologise’: Tamil Nadu govt to Supreme Court on temple lamp row
points: Madurai collector Nishant Krishna apologised to the Supreme Court on Wednesday for failing to carry out its order allowing a ceremonial lamp to be lit at a disputed stone pillar at Thirupparankundram Hill, but blamed the temple board for not complying with…
“I sincerely apologise for the lamp not been lit at the Deepathoon,” the Madurai collector said in his status report to the top court.

Krishna said he had taken “all the steps” between November 21 and 24 to secure the Devasthanam’s authorisation for a team to light the lamp at the stone pillar, known as the Deepathoon, in line with the court’s November 20 order.
“However, the Board of Trustees, by its resolution dated 24.11.2026, resolved to light the lamp at the customary place.

On November 20, a bench of justices Aravind Kumar and VM Pancholi permitted the lighting of the lamp on the stone pillar at Thirupparankundram Hill on Karthigai Deepam day as a restricted, one-time measure only.

items.title: Shapoor Mistry lobbied Modi twice for Tata Sons IPO as battle over listing intensifies
points: Shapoor Mistry, the head of the Shapoorji Pallonji Group, has reached out to Prime Minister Modi regarding the listing troubles faced by Tata Sons.
He claims that Tata Trusts are obstructing the public offering for their own benefit and breaching regulations.
Meanwhile, the Reserve Bank of India has pressured Tata Sons to meet listing necessities.

items.title: 'No reason to interfere with govt decision': Delhi HC refuses to reopen Kartarpur Corridor
points: The Delhi High Court on Wednesday refused to direct the Centre to reopen the Kartarpur Corridor, holding that its closure following the April 22, 2025, Pahalgam terror attack was a policy decision taken in the interest of citizens.

A bench of acting chief justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma said there was “no reason to interfere with the government’s decision”, while leaving it to the authorities to consider a representation seeking the corridor’s reopening.

The court was hearing a petition filed by the Paardarshita Public Welfare Foundation, which sought the reopening of the corridor to allow Sikh pilgrims to visit Gurdwara Darbar Sahib in Kartarpur, Pakistan.
The bench noted that the Centre had decided to suspend the corridor from May 7, 2025, following the Pahalgam terror attack, in which 26 people were killed.
The Kartarpur Corridor was inaugurated on November 9, 2019, to mark the 550th birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev.

items.title: PhonePe resumes IPO process; targets February-March listing at $12-15 billion valuation
points: PhonePe has resumed its initial public offering plans after deferring them due to market uncertainties.
The company aims for a stock market listing valued between USD 12-15 billion in early 2024.
It expects to raise approximately Rs 12,000-14,000 crore through an offer-for-sale.
The digital payments firm has also reported significant revenue growth and is now profitable at the group level.

items.title: Gold price prediction: Despite 27% decline from January peak, UBS still retains ₹1.50 lakh/10 gram target for 2027

items.title: Neda makes VLCC comeback with Chinese order
points: Greek shipowner Neda Maritime Agency has returned to the VLCC newbuilding market, lining up one firm vessel and an option for another at China’s New Times Shipbuilding.
Shipbrokers have linked the Lykiardopoulos family-controlled company to a deal for 303,000 dwt crude carriers at the Jiangsu-based yard, with both vessels pencilled in for delivery in 2030.
Pricing has not emerged, although similar-sized VLCCs recently booked at the same yard have been valued by shipbrokers at around $130m apiece.
The move marks Neda’s first reported VLCC newbuilding investment since September 2019, when it ordered a 300,000 dwt tanker at South Korea’s HD Hyundai Samho.
The Piraeus-based owner had previously turned to the same Korean yard in 2017 for the 300,000 dwt Ascona, which joined its fleet in January 2019.
Neda currently manages nine tankers, comprising five VLCCs and four aframaxes, alongside 16 dry bulk carriers.

items.title: USD ≈7bn lost per year: the hidden cost of how shipping trades
points: Shipping is no stranger to transformation.

From the cargo owner’s perspective, the study identifies and quantifies around USD 7bn a year in potentially avoidable costs across dry bulk and product tanker shipping.
The inefficiencies range from vessels waiting to berth and ships that are not loaded to full capacity, to contracts that do not reward efficiency.
Klaveness believes the full potential could reach USD 10–20bn a year, or 5–10% of the roughly USD 190bn spent on freight in the two segments.
The study reviewed around 50 possible sources of inefficiency and examined 14 in depth, so roughly half of the potential is still to be explored.
The USD 7bn is an indicative sum of individual estimates, with some overlap, and is not a savings forecast.

points: OpenAI and Cisco have introduced Shirudo, an open-source security tool that aims to protect Linux systems from cyberattacks while developers work on permanent fixes.
The tool uses eBPF technology to block attempts to exploit known vulnerabilities without taking applications offline or restarting systems.
Shirudo uses eBPF, a Linux technology that allows small programmes to run at specific points inside the operating system, according to the announcement.
OpenAI and Cisco have designed Shirudo to support AI agents that can investigate vulnerabilities, develop shields and test them against exploits and real workloads.
In a controlled test, the coding agent created a shield against a Java4Shell exploit targeting a running Elasticsearch service.

items.title: Royal Navy Submarine That Disappeared With 64 Crew While Patrolling The Aegean Sea

Historical records support this theory as a German minelayer laid approximately 287 mines in the area before the arrival of the Trooper, which was being commanded by John S.Wraith, a lieutenant with the Royal Navy.
It left Beirut in September 1943 to patrol close to the Dodecanese, a group of islands off Turkiye, which are now part of Greece but were under the control of Italy during that time.

Vande Mataram at J&K waqf event sparks row
points: Several Muslim clerics who attended a Waqf Board event in Srinagar expressed their regret after Vande Mataram was played.
They said their participation did not endorse the song, and they prayed for forgiveness.
The song sparked controversy as it allegedly conflicts with Islamic principles of Tawheed, promoting the oneness of Allah.
The Mutahida Majlis-e-Ulama criticised the Waqf Board for playing Vande Mataram at a Muslim institution.

items.title: Omar government breaks silence on Sheshnag row, says lake safe
points: The J&K government asserted that Sheshnag Lake remains completely safe following allegations of construction by the Border Roads Organisation.
Forest minister Altaf Kaloo reported that heavy machinery operated away from the lake, ensuring no soil entered the water body.
A 12-member inspection team found no tampering with the lake's track as maintenance is performed before the Amarnath Yatra.

items.title: PM Modi wants ITI courses aligned with industry needs, jobs closer to home
points: PM Narendra Modi emphasized the need for public sector undertakings to establish connections with Industrial Training Institutes.
He highlighted the importance of a 'Classroom–Company–Career' approach to enhance employment opportunities for youth.
Modi suggested that PSUs should evaluate future manpower needs and strengthen partnership with ITIs to recruit trained candidates.
He also encouraged decentralised solar and wind power projects closer to consumption centers.

items.title: Cheeni Kum: Poor monsoon hits sugar crop, gross output may not meet domestic need
points: India's sugar production for the 2026-27 season is expected to decrease by 15%, primarily due to weather issues.
Maharashtra and Karnataka will contribute significantly to the decline following inadequate rainfall.
The expected net sugar production will be around 265 lakh tonne, down from nearly 280 lakh tonne last season.
Indian Sugar & Bio-Energy Manufacturers Association noted various climatic factors affecting sugar crops across key states.

Government’s big manufacturing push: Rs 11,000 crore for infrastructure equipment, six new urea plants
points: The Indian government approved a new scheme to promote domestic manufacturing of construction and infrastructure equipment.
This scheme will incentivize the production of advanced machinery over eight years, reducing import dependence.
Additionally, six new brownfield urea plants have been cleared to boost domestic agricultural production.
These plants aim to enhance urea production to meet national demand and cut imports.

Delhi SIR: Nearly 44 lakh voters may remain off final electoral roll after low Form 6 turnout
points: Nearly 44 lakh voters are at risk of remaining excluded from Delhi's final electoral roll.
Only about 3.5 lakh Form 6 applications have been submitted by the deadline.
Efforts to trace voters categorized as absent, shifted, deceased, or duplicate have seen limited success due to various challenges.
The distribution of enumeration forms is ongoing and will conclude at the end of November.

PRAGATI meeting: PM Modi reviews infrastructure projects worth over Rs 78,000 crore, stresses timely execution
points: Prime Minister Narendra Modi led a review meeting on key infrastructure projects worth over Rs 78,000 crore.
The discussion included strategies to enhance road, railway, power, and coal sectors while addressing delays and implementation issues.
A significant focus was placed on improving the Industrial Training Institute ecosystem through the PM-SETU initiative.
Partnerships between industries and ITIs were encouraged to align training with job market demands.

items.title: PM Modi asks ministers to stay put & stay ready; next Parliament session likely before December 15: Report
points: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has directed ministers to avoid foreign travel and prepare for the upcoming Parliament session.
The Cabinet meeting highlighted delays in convening the Winter Session, which has raised questions from opposition parties.
The government's focus is on possibly introducing the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill linked to delimitation and women's reservation in Parliament.
Changes in political alliances have altered required support dynamics for passing legislation.

items.title: MSME sector: Govt sets 50% registration target for women entrepreneurs
points: In a significant move, Union MSME minister Jitan Ram Manjhi shared plans to boost women's registration in Udyam to an ambitious 50%.
He highlighted that embracing inclusivity within the MSME sector is crucial for driving economic advancement.

Furthermore, the government is dedicated to creating enhanced opportunities for entrepreneurs from marginalized backgrounds, prioritizing access to funding, technology integration, and fortifying global competitiveness across various identified growth sectors.

Aero India 2027 expands exhibition space as demand exceeds capacity
points: The Ministry of Defence is set to enhance the exhibition infrastructure for Aero India 2027 due to growing interest in the event.
Scheduled for February 2027 at Air Force Station Yelahanka, the exhibition will feature two new hangars and optional mezzanine floors for exhibitors.
These developments will allow a wider array of international aerospace firms and domestic producers to display their innovations effectively.

Amid SIR complaints, EC directs states to correct voter list errors
points: The Election Commission has mandated that officials focus on rectifying inaccuracies in the electoral rolls during the revision phase.
Voter information currently on file will be cross-referenced with new data gathered from a Special Intensive Revision process.
Booth level officers will validate voter information and process Form 8 applications when needed.
Necessary updates to personal information must follow the approved Form 8 after verification.

items.title: 'No significant impact on India': MeitY secretary on US chip export curbs
points: Krishnan, secretary of MeitY, reassured that the recent US chip export restrictions won't impact India.
He stated that India is appreciated as a reliable partner in data centre technology.
In addition, over 200 companies have expressed interest in the India Semiconductor Mission 2.0.
Krishnan also mentioned the exciting advancements of Chariot One, an innovative text-to-speech AI model developed by Indian graduates, showcasing India's technological prowess.
